title: What is Gold Hallmarking & Importance of Mandatory Compliance
content: Hallmarking is the accurate determination and official recording of the proportionate content of precious metal (gold or silver) in jewellery and artefacts. Under the Hallmarking Order issued by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, hallmarking is mandatory across notified districts in India. Its primary objective is to safeguard consumers against adulteration and under-caratage, ensure honest trade practices, and establish third-party verified purity standards.
source_name: Bureau of Indian Standards & Department of Consumer Affairs
section: Mandatory Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery Orders

title: The 3 Mandatory Marks on Hallmarked Gold Jewellery
content: Every piece of hallmarked gold jewellery sold in India must bear 3 distinct laser-engraved marks: 1) The BIS Standard Logo: A triangular mark signifying BIS certification; 2) Purity in Karat and Fineness: Approved grades such as 24K999 (99.9%), 23K958 (95.8%), 22K916 (91.6%), 20K833 (83.3%), 18K750 (75.0%), or 14K585 (58.5%); 3) Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID): A unique 6-digit alphanumeric code laser-inscribed on each individual jewellery piece at a BIS-recognized Assaying and Hallmarking Centre (AHC).
document_title: IS 1417: 2016 (Gold and Gold Alloys, Jewellery/Artefacts - Fineness and Marking)

title: What is HUID & How Consumers Can Verify Hallmarked Jewellery
content: HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) is a unique 6-digit alphanumeric code laser-engraved on every single piece of gold jewellery during assaying at a BIS-recognized Assaying and Hallmarking Centre (AHC). HUID ensures complete traceability. Consumers can verify any hallmarked article using the 'Verify HUID' feature on the official BIS Care mobile app. Entering the 6-character code displays: 1) Jeweller's registration number and business name, 2) Assaying and Hallmarking Centre (AHC) details, 3) Date of hallmarking, and 4) Article type and purity grade.
document_title: BIS Care Mobile Application User Guide & HUID System Manual

title: Consumer Redressal & Compensation for Substandard Hallmarked Jewellery
content: Under Rule 49 of the Bureau of Indian Standards Rules, 2018, if hallmarked jewellery is tested at a BIS-recognized Assaying and Hallmarking Centre (AHC) and found to have a lower purity than marked, the registered jeweller is legally obligated to compensate the consumer. The compensation payable is calculated as two times the difference in value based on the shortage of purity for the weight of the article sold, plus full reimbursement of the testing charges incurred by the consumer.
